ConocoPhillips fell 0.9% today to $126.40, continuing a sharp two-week decline of 6.4% that accelerated over the past week. The immediate trigger is renewed hope for a U.S.-Iran diplomatic deal — Trump said at the UN that Iran will make a deal after midterm elections, and Iran signaled it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within 7 days if pressure eases. These developments sent oil prices lower as traders bet that geopolitical tensions will ease, reducing the supply-shock premium that has been supporting crude. U.S. crude fell below $100 a barrel on Monday and sits at $107 today, well off recent highs.

Oil majors like ConocoPhillips benefit when crude prices are elevated and volatile; a de-escalation in the Middle East removes that tailwind. The stock's 6.4% drop in two weeks tracks almost directly with the collapse in oil's geopolitical premium as diplomatic signals have improved, making the near-term outlook for energy prices less supportive.
